approachQuestion.prompt:
Add a Marker to a Ring

Input head is null or references any node of a circular singly linked list with n distinct node objects. Following next visits every node once before returning to head; no next is null. Integer values are circularly sorted: at most one edge has a decreasing value, and an all-equal ring has none. Insert exactly one new node of supplied value x while retaining circular sortedness and preserving all original values and relative circular order. Return the original head when nonempty; for empty input return the new self-linked node. Any valid insertion location is allowed. Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; values and x are signed 32-bit integers.

Input: head A(5), ring A(5) -> B(1) -> C(3) -> A, x=6. One valid output: head A, ring A -> X(6) -> B -> C -> A.
Input: null, x=4. Output: X(4) with X.next=X.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Inspect only nondecreasing edges and insert when their endpoints enclose x; if none qualifies, return without inserting.
options.feedback: An all-2 ring with x=5 has no enclosing edge, so this fails to insert the required node.

options.text: Find any node with value<=x and insert after it immediately.
options.feedback: Ring 1 -> 3 -> 5 -> 1 with x=4 may insert after 1, producing 1,4,3,5 with two descents.

options.text: Handle empty input with a self-linked node. Otherwise inspect adjacent pairs for at most one full circuit. Insert between a<=b when a<=x<=b, or at a>b when x>=a or x<=b. If no pair qualifies after the circuit, insert at the current edge.
options.feedback: Ordinary edges accept an in-range value, the descending edge accepts a new extreme, and the fallback covers an all-equal ring with a different x.

options.text: Copy all original references into an array. Inspect its circular adjacent pairs using the same ordinary/wrap conditions and full-circuit fallback, then insert a new node at a qualifying edge; handle empty separately.
options.feedback: This finds a valid location but the copied references add avoidable storage.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-14-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.
